title: Routine transesophageal echocardiography in severe aortic stenosis
summary:
The most common heart valve disease in old age is aortic valve stenosis. The severity is classified using a cardiac ultrasound examination, in which the valve opening area is derived using mathematical approaches. An oral ultrasound examination is only recommended if the image quality is poor.
There are advantages and disadvantages to transesophageal echocardiography.  The advantages include better assessment of calcification, thickening, and mobility of the valve leaflets, as well as possible deposits on the valve. Transesophageal echocardiography can be decisive in cases of unclear findings.
A disadvantage is the higher risk of injury to the esophagus. A recent study shows a high degree of agreement between the measurements obtained using the mathematical approach and those obtained by measuring the area.
Imaging techniques such as computed tomography show valid results with regard to anatomical structures and the degree of calcification.
The study aims to investigate the clinical value of routinely performed transesophageal echocardiography in cases of severe aortic valve stenosis.
To this end, existing ultrasound findings (external and transesophageal echocardiography) from 8 years (July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2025) will be evaluated.

interventions.name:
The aim of this study is to investigate the clinical impact of routine TEE in addition to TTE for the management of patients with suspected severe aortic stenosis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with suspected or confirmed severe aortic valve stenosis, i.e. patients with severe or moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis on TTE.
Exclusion criteria:
• Absence of either TEE or TTE
• Insufficient image quality to obtain AVA (aortic valve area) or mean gradient (dP mean)
• Patients with suspected severe but confirmed moderate aortic stenosis by in-hospital TTE (without TEE)
• Persons <18 years old (aortic stenosis is a disease of elderly patients. Atherosclerotic aortic stenosis does not occur in adolescents)
